notes: Summary: BlueHarbor Insurance Labs evaluating Redwood Dedicated for mission-critical agent-assist and document search workloads. Primary ask: predictable p95 latency, guaranteed throughput during peak claims windows, and explicit cross-region failover without violating EU data residency for EU customers.
Workload profile and requirements:

- Agent UI: conversational assistant used by claims adjusters. Target: p95 <= 250ms for short-turn Q&A (<= 512 tokens), steady concurrency target ~400 sessions during US business hours, spike handling up to 1200 concurrent sessions during surge windows.
- Bulk document search/embeddings: nightly re-embed of ~10M docs, throughput tolerance for batch jobs but strict SLA for realtime search of policy docs (p95 <= 500ms).
- Reranking/fraud-scoring: tight tail latency required for critical scoring pipeline; prefer model variant fallback to smaller quantized model under saturation.
Dedicated capacity planning discussed:
- Baseline recommendation from SE: reserve 8x A100-80GB equivalents (mix of A100 and A10 where feasible) to meet steady concurrency with 2x safety buffer for KV cache churn and warmup.

- Autoscaling policy: strong preference for reserved baseline with burst pool for short surges (<=15 minutes). Customer wants guaranteed burst capacity in contract (burst tokens per month + per-second throttle guarantees).
- Warmup and cold start: need pre-warming for overnight batch windows and canary warm pools to avoid cold KV-cache penalties.
SLO/SLA negotiation points (customer redlines):
- Deterministic p95 latency target scoped per route and model. They want contractual p95 + credits for misses and a clear definition (exclude scheduled maintenance windows).
- Throughput guarantees: requests/sec per reserved GPU at different sequence lengths; ask to include a degradation plan rather than silent throttling.

- Cross-region failover: explicit RTO <= 10 minutes for region failure, read-only failover for EU-resident data unless customer authorizes full replication. Also require data residency control to keep EU PII in-region during normal operation.
Reliability & fallback design specifics discussed (technical):

- Model variant fallback: on saturation, route traffic to smaller quantized variants (e.g., 70B fp16 -> 13B q4) with output-quality labeling and flagging downstream. Customer wants automatic circuit-breaker + manual override from console.
- Smart routing: prefer policy to route EU-origin traffic to EU Dedicated region; in failover event, tokenization of PII and consent flows must be enforced before cross-region processing.
- Cache-first strategy: use prefix/KV caching for agent context to reduce compute and improve tail latency. SE proposed per-customer KV allocations and cache hit SLAs.
- Canary and progressive rollouts: will require canary traffic slice (1-5%) for model upgrades and fallback runbooks with observability for prompt regressions.
POC results and open technical questions:
- POC: 4x A100 baseline showed p95 ~220ms for 256-token completions with batching enabled. Under synthetic concurrency spike (x3), p95 jumped to 820ms and request queuing observed.

- Open question: exact mapping of reserved GPU counts to guaranteed requests/sec at different seq lengths and batching profiles. Customer requested a capacity calculator and deterministic acceptance test harness.
- Open question: acceptable quality drop thresholds for automatic fallback to smaller models; customer requires test prompts+gold outputs to be included in SLA for regression monitoring.
Commercial asks / negotiation items:
- Contract must include: reserved GPU count, guaranteed burst capacity, explicit cross-region failover clauses, credits for missed latency SLOs, and data residency guarantees.
- Pricing ask: prefer blended committed rate for 12 months with quarterly review. Also asked for optional on-prem connector licensing for high-security sites.
Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-15: Technical workshop (SEs + infra + customer SREs) to produce capacity calculator and deterministic acceptance tests.
- Legal: Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO artifacts and draft SLA with explicit RTO/RPO language by 2026-03-22.
- POC tuning: SE to run second perf sweep with 8x A100 reserved config and KV-cache warmup scripts; capture p50/p95/p99 and throughput at planned concurrency (due 2026-03-21).
Stated customer quote (paraphrase): 'We can tolerate small quality dips during extreme saturation if we have transparency, routing control, and a predictable recovery plan.'
